801: additively.  Define
802: \begin{equation}\label{eq:beta-corrected-new}
803:  \begin{aligned}
804:   \beta_t^{\rm corr}
805:   &=\sqrt{\gamma_{t-1}+2\log(1/\delta)}+\sqrt\lambda S\\
806:   &\quad+\frac1\sigma\sqrt{\sum_{s<t}
807:   [\epsilon_{\rm lin}(s)+\epsilon_{\rm mis}(s)]^2}.
808:  \end{aligned}
809: \end{equation}
810: 
811: The radius contains the stochastic uncertainty term, the ridge penalty for
812: the reference parameter, and the accumulated historical approximation error.
813: The following result supplies the reference-confidence band required by
814: \Cref{asm:abstract-transport}.
815: 
816: \begin{corollary}[Corrected-center confidence without optimizer assumptions]
817: \label{cor:corrected-center-new}
818: With probability at least $1-\delta$, simultaneously over rounds and actions,
819: \begin{equation}\label{eq:corrected-confidence-new}
820:  |\mu_t^*(a)-m_t^{\rm corr}(a)|
821:  \le\beta_t^{\rm corr}\bar s_t(a)
822:  +\epsilon_{\rm lin,t}(a)+\epsilon_{\rm mis,t}(a).
823: \end{equation}
824: The identity and bound hold for any predictable $\btheta_t$ in the certified
825: region.  They require no exact ERM, approximate stationarity, optimizer
826: residual, or optimizer convergence rate.
827: \end{corollary}
828: 
829: The historical deterministic term in \eqref{eq:beta-corrected-new} follows from
830: $\Phi_t^\top\bVbar_t^{-1}\Phi_t\preceq I$ for
831: $\Phi_t=[\bq_1/\sigma,\ldots,\bq_{t-1}/\sigma]$.  Its scaling is
832: $1/\sigma$, not $1/\sigma^2$.  Fixed nonvanishing misspecification generally
833: creates a linear current-bias term and can also make the historical radius
834: vacuous.  This is a graceful-degradation statement, not a robust
835: misspecified-bandit guarantee.
836: 
837: \section{When the regret bound is informative}
838: \label{sec:closed-rates-new}
839: 
840: The general theorem depends on quantities accumulated along the policy's
841: history.  This section replaces the information gain by a bound in terms of
842: parameter dimension and horizon, then asks when the remaining transport and
843: approximation terms are controlled.  A valid certificate alone is not enough:
844: a large historical error radius or persistent current bias can still prevent
845: the displayed regret bound from being sublinear.
846: 
847: \paragraph{Bound information gain using dimension.}
848: Let $r_T=\min\{d,T\}$.  The frozen Gram matrix has at most this rank above
849: its ridge term.  Bounding its eigenvalue sum using the query-norm bound gives
850: \begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-d-gamma-new}
851:  \gamma_T\le\Gamma_{T,d}:=
852:  r_T\log\!\left(1+\frac{TG^2}{r_T\lambda\sigma^2}\right).
853: \end{equation}
854: No fixed tangent subspace is required.  The next corollary substitutes this
855: bound and the corrected-center radius into the general theorem.  Its
856: $B_T$ collects historical error energy, while $E_T^{\rm cur}$ collects the
857: current prediction-error allowances.
858: 
859: \begin{corollary}[Finite-dimensional corrected-center rate]
860: \label{cor:finite-d-rate-new}
861: Suppose $\bar D_t\le D$, $\alpha_t\le\alpha$, and
862: $\kappa_{+,t}/\kappa_{-,t}\le K$ for all $t$.  Let
863: \begin{align*}
864:  B_T&=\sum_{s<T}[\epsilon_{\rm lin}(s)+\epsilon_{\rm mis}(s)]^2,\\
865:  E_T^{\rm cur}&=\sum_{t=1}^T
866:  [\epsilon_{\rm lin,t}(a_t)+\epsilon_{\rm mis,t}(a_t)].
867: \end{align*}
868: Then \Cref{thm:transported-ucb,cor:corrected-center-new} imply
869: \begin{align}
870: R_T
871: &\le2\alpha e^D\sqrt K\nonumber\\
872: &\quad{}\times
873: \left[\sqrt{\Gamma_{T,d}+2\log(1/\delta)}+\sqrt\lambda S
874: +\frac{\sqrt{B_T}}{\sigma}\right]\nonumber\\
875: &\quad{}\times
876: \sqrt{\left(\sigma^2+\frac{G^2}{\lambda}\right)T\Gamma_{T,d}}
877: \nonumber\\
878: &\quad+2E_T^{\rm cur}+\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t.
879: \label{eq:finite-d-rate-new-display}
880: \end{align}
881: With exact realizability and a frozen linear model, $B_T=E_T^{\rm cur}=0$.
882: For fixed $d$ and problem constants, the leading term is then
883: $O(e^D\sqrt K\,d\sqrt T\log T)$.  Exact solves set $\alpha=1$, exact current
884: curvature sets $K=1$, and exact score maximization sets $\xi_t=0$, recovering
885: the standard LinUCB determinant-potential rate up to displayed constants.
886: \end{corollary}
887: 
888: \paragraph{Control both transport and linearization error.}
889: The preceding bound becomes useful when the transport factors stay controlled
890: and the approximation errors are small enough.  The next corollary gives a
891: sufficient regime: the model is nearly linear throughout a certified parameter
892: region.  Its scale $W$ controls both gradient change and Taylor error.  The
893: condition relates this scale to the horizon; it is not a statement that an
894: arbitrary fixed nonlinear model has sublinear regret.
895: 
896: \begin{corollary}[Global near-linearity under exponential transport]
897: \label{cor:global-near-linear-new}
898: Assume exact realizability, $\mu^*(z)=\mu_{\btheta^\circ}(z)$, and suppose
899: $\|\btheta^\circ\|_2\le R$ and $\|\btheta_t\|_2\le R$ for every $t$.
900: On the certified convex radius-$R$ region, assume the prediction gradient is
901: $L_\mu$-Lipschitz for the Taylor envelopes and satisfies the replay-path
902: Hessian bound $L_g$ in \Cref{cor:hessian-path-new}, with
903: \[
904:  L_\mu\le\frac{c_\mu}{\sqrt W},\qquad
905:  L_g\le\frac{c_g}{\sqrt W},
906: \]
907: with $W>0$.  Use the corrected center, exact current curvature, exact dense
908: solves, and exact score maximization in finite parameter dimension $d$, and
909: suppose $\|\bq_t(a)\|_2\le G$.  Thus
910: $\alpha_t=1$, $\kappa_{-,t}=\kappa_{+,t}=1$, and $\xi_t=0$.
911: Define
912: \[
913:  D_{T,W}:=\frac{4c_gR\sqrt{T-1}}{\sigma\sqrt{\lambda W}}.
914: \]
915: Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$,
916: \begin{align}
917:  R_T
918:  &\le 2e^{D_{T,W}}
919:  \Biggl[
920:  \begin{aligned}
921:   &\sqrt{\Gamma_{T,d}+2\log(1/\delta)}+\sqrt\lambda R\\[-1mm]
922:   &\quad+\frac{2c_\mu R^2\sqrt T}{\sigma\sqrt W}
923:  \end{aligned}
924:  \Biggr]\nonumber\\[-1mm]
925:  &\quad\times
926:  \sqrt{\sigma^2+\frac{G^2}{\lambda}}\,
927:  \sqrt{T\Gamma_{T,d}}\nonumber\\
928:  &\quad+\frac{4c_\mu R^2T}{\sqrt W}.
929:  \label{eq:global-near-linear-new}
930: \end{align}
931: Consequently, $W=\Omega(T)$ with a sufficiently large problem-dependent
932: constant keeps $D_{T,W}=O(1)$.  For fixed $d$ and fixed problem constants,
933: \[
934:  R_T=O(d\sqrt T\log T)+O(\sqrt T).
935: \]
936: This conclusion requires no $D_t<1$ condition.  Here $W$ is an abstract
937: near-linearity scale, not generic network width or parameter count, and the
938: result is not an unrestricted neural-training theorem.  No optimizer-residual
939: rate is required because the corrected center is used.
940: \end{corollary}
941: 
942: \begin{remark}[Comparable guarantees do not order policies]
943: \Cref{prop:frozen-width-ucb,cor:corrected-center-new} give a frozen-width
944: counterpart to \eqref{eq:finite-d-rate-new-display}, with the factor
945: $\alpha e^D\sqrt K$ removed and all remaining quantities evaluated on the
946: frozen policy's own history.  With the same $\lambda$, $\sigma$, and
947: confidence level, common uniform bounds on the query norm, reference norm,
948: approximation envelopes, and accumulated oracle error give guarantees of the
949: same order when $D$, $\alpha$, and $K$ are bounded.  In particular, under the
950: statistical, uniform-region, and smoothness assumptions of
951: \Cref{cor:global-near-linear-new}, the corrected center and exact
952: frozen-width score maximization give the same
953: $O(d\sqrt T\log T)+O(\sqrt T)$ rate when $W=\Omega(T)$, for fixed $d$
954: and fixed problem constants.
955: This comparison does not rank realized regret: different selected actions
956: change the representation paths, centers, radii, and information gains.
957: It neither proves that transport is unnecessary nor rules out improved
958: performance from current curvature.  The stated $W$ scaling is a sufficient
959: condition for these bounds, not a necessary condition for an informative
960: transport certificate.
961: \end{remark}
962: 
963: \paragraph{A concrete model with fixed feature directions.}
964: The scaled-tanh model makes the smoothness condition explicit.  It also has
965: more structure than the general Hessian argument uses: changing the parameter
966: rescales each feature gradient without rotating its direction.  This permits
967: the sharper endpoint comparison developed after the model's derivative
968: formulas.
969: 
970: \begin{remark}[Scaled-tanh specialization]
971: For
972: \[
973:  \mu_{\btheta,W}(z)=\sqrt W\tanh\!\left(
974:  \frac{\phi(z)^\top\btheta}{\sqrt W}\right),
975:  \qquad \|\phi(z)\|_2\le B_\phi,
976: \]
977: write $u=\phi(z)^\top\btheta/\sqrt W$.  Then
978: \begin{align*}
979:  \nabla_\theta\mu_{\btheta,W}(z)
980:  &=\operatorname{sech}^2(u)\phi(z),\\
981:  \nabla_\theta^2\mu_{\btheta,W}(z)
982:  &=-\frac{2}{\sqrt W}\operatorname{sech}^2(u)\tanh(u)
983:  \phi(z)\phi(z)^\top.
984: \end{align*}
985: Since
986: $\sup_u|2\operatorname{sech}^2(u)\tanh(u)|=4/(3\sqrt3)$,
987: \Cref{cor:global-near-linear-new} applies with
988: \[
989:  G=B_\phi,\qquad
990:  c_\mu=c_g=c_h:=\frac{4B_\phi^2}{3\sqrt3}.
991: \]
992: The symbol $W$ is a smoothness scale here; it is not identified with hidden
993: width or parameter count.
994: \end{remark}
995: 
996: \paragraph{Compare scalar weights instead of accumulating a path bound.}
997: For a fixed observation, the gradients at collection time and at the current
998: parameter point in the same feature direction.  Their contributions to the
999: Gram matrix differ only by the \emph{squares} of their scalar gradient
1000: multipliers.  Bounds on the ratio of these weights therefore compare the
1001: endpoint matrices directly.  The common ridge term must be included in that
1002: comparison as well.
1003: 
1004: There are two versions.  A uniform bound uses only the parameter and feature
1005: norm bounds.  When observations share a finite collection of feature vectors,
1006: a category-wise bound uses the accumulated collection-time weight and the
1007: current weight within each category.  Both are certificates for the same
1008: reference-confidence construction; neither supplies a new statistical event.
1009: 
1010: \begin{corollary}[Relative weights for scaled tanh]
1011: \label{cor:tanh-relative-weights}
1012: For the scaled-tanh model above, suppose $W>0$, $\|\phi(z_s)\|_2\le B_\phi$,
1013: and $\|\btheta_s\|_2,\|\btheta_t\|_2\le R$ for all $s<t$.
1014: Set $\omega_\theta(z)=\operatorname{sech}^2(\phi(z)^\top\theta/\sqrt W)$ and
1015: $\ell=\operatorname{sech}^2(B_\phi R/\sqrt W)>0$.  For
1016: \begin{align*}
1017:  \bVbar_t&=\lambda\bI+\sigma^{-2}\sum_{s<t}
1018:  \omega_{\btheta_s}(z_s)^2\phi(z_s)\phi(z_s)^\top,\\
1019:  \bV_t&=\lambda\bI+\sigma^{-2}\sum_{s<t}
1020:  \omega_{\btheta_t}(z_s)^2\phi(z_s)\phi(z_s)^\top,
1021: \end{align*}
1022: the uniform endpoint certificate is
1023: \begin{equation}\label{eq:tanh-uniform-relative}
1024:  \ell^2\bVbar_t\preceq\bV_t\preceq\ell^{-2}\bVbar_t,
1025:  \qquad d_{\rm Th}(\bVbar_t,\bV_t)
1026:  \le4\log\cosh(B_\phi R/\sqrt W).
1027: \end{equation}
1028: If the observed feature vectors belong to a finite set $\{\phi_c\}$, let
1029: $n_{t,c}$ be their counts, let
1030: $f_{t,c}=\sum_{s<t:\phi(z_s)=\phi_c}\omega_{\btheta_s}(z_s)^2$, and put
1031: $g_{t,c}=n_{t,c}\operatorname{sech}^4(\phi_c^\top\btheta_t/\sqrt W)$.
1032: The sharper category certificate is
1033: \begin{equation}\label{eq:tanh-category-relative}
1034:  c_{-,t}=\min\!\left\{1,\min_{c:n_{t,c}>0}\frac{g_{t,c}}{f_{t,c}}\right\},
1035:  \qquad
1036:  c_{+,t}=\max\!\left\{1,\max_{c:n_{t,c}>0}\frac{g_{t,c}}{f_{t,c}}\right\},
1037: \end{equation}
1038: with $c_{-,1}=c_{+,1}=1$ for an empty history.  It satisfies
1039: \eqref{eq:relative-endpoint-sandwich} and
1040: $\ell^2\le c_{-,t}\le1\le c_{+,t}\le\ell^{-2}$.
1041: Either certificate can be used in \Cref{cor:relative-endpoint-ucb}.
1042: \end{corollary}
1043: 
1044: The uniform bound has no explicit horizon dependence when its norm bounds and
1045: $W$ are fixed.  This controls transport, but does not remove the separate
1046: historical and current approximation errors from the regret bound.
1047: For the category version, maintaining a count and a collection-weight sum
1048: per category lets \eqref{eq:tanh-category-relative} use current category
1049: projections without an eigensolve or a scan of the full history.  It reduces
1050: the work needed for this certificate, not the cost of all width or center
1051: solves.  The construction relies on fixed gradient directions and does not
1052: cover general gradient rotation or establish improved policy regret.
1053: The appendix gives the termwise proof and an example where the endpoint
1054: distance is zero although the synthetic path has positive length.
1055: 
1056: \paragraph{A local comparison when changes are small.}
1057: A local two-sided comparison gives another way to relate the same matrices.
1058: It replaces the exponential factors by a local sandwich that requires a
1059: smallness condition.
1060: If $\chi_t<1$ and
1061: \begin{equation}\label{eq:local-additive-new}
1062:  (1-\chi_t)^2\bVbar_t\preceq\bV_t
1063:  \preceq(1+\chi_t)^2\bVbar_t,
1064: \end{equation}
1065: use the local score obtained from \eqref{eq:transported-score-new} by replacing
1066: $e^{\bar D_t/2}$ with $1+\chi_t$.
1067: \begin{corollary}[Local small-drift transport]
1068: \label{cor:local-small-drift-new}
1069: Under the remaining hypotheses of \Cref{thm:transported-ucb}, the local score
1070: satisfies
1071: \begin{align}
1072: R_T
1073: &\le\sqrt{\left(\sigma^2+\frac{G^2}{\lambda}\right)\gamma_T
1074: \sum_{t=1}^T\beta_t^2
1075: \left[1+\alpha_t\frac{1+\chi_t}{1-\chi_t}
1076: \sqrt{\frac{\kappa_{+,t}}{\kappa_{-,t}}}\right]^2}
1077: \nonumber\\
1078: &\quad+2\sum_{t=1}^Tb_t(a_t)+\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t.
1079: \label{eq:local-small-drift-regret-new}
1080: \end{align}
1081: \end{corollary}
1082: Neither the local factor nor the exponential factor uniformly dominates the
1083: other because they summarize different paths.

1114: \paragraph{What remains model-specific.}
1115: The geometric comparisons can be reused with another estimator if it supplies
1116: \eqref{eq:abstract-confidence-new}.  Geometry alone does not supply that
1117: statistical premise.  For an exponential-family model, one would also need a
1118: likelihood-score confidence event, a conversion to prediction error,
1119: pre-reward collection-time Fisher weights, control of weight and Jacobian
1120: transport, and an information-potential bound.  Those additional steps are
1121: outside the squared-loss specialization established here.
